title: 01. Foundations: Python Virtual Environment (Windows)
summary: A venv is an isolated Python environment — like a clean room for each project. Each project gets its own packages without conflicting with others.

sections.title: What is a Virtual Environment?
sections.body:
> A **venv** is an isolated Python environment — like a clean room for each project. Each project gets its own packages without conflicting with others.

```
WITHOUT VENV:                    WITH VENV:
                                 
Your PC                          Your PC
└── Python (global)              ├── Python (global)
    └── openai==0.28 ❌           ├── project_a/venv/
        conflicts!                │   └── openai==1.0  ✅
        langchain broken          └── project_b/venv/
                                      └── openai==0.28 ✅
```

sections.title: Step-by-Step Windows venv Guide
sections.body:
```bash
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 1: Open Command Prompt or PowerShell
# Press Windows + R → type "cmd" → Enter
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# STEP 2: Navigate to your project folder
cd C:\Users\YourName\Documents
mkdir genai_project          # Create new folder
cd genai_project             # Go into it

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 3: CHECK Python is installed
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
python --version
# Should show: Python 3.10.x or higher

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 4: CREATE the virtual environment
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
python -m venv venv
# This creates a "venv" folder in your project directory
# Structure created:
# genai_project/
# └── venv/
#     ├── Scripts/      ← Windows (activate is here)
#     ├── Lib/
#     └── pyvenv.cfg

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 5: ACTIVATE the virtual environment
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# In Command Prompt (CMD):
venv\Scripts\activate

# In PowerShell:
venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# If PowerShell gives error, run this first:
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
# Then activate again:
venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

```

# ✅ SUCCESS! You'll see (venv) at the start of your prompt:
# (venv) C:\Users\YourName\Documents\genai_project>

# STEP 6: INSTALL packages (inside venv)
pip install openai groq anthropic tiktoken numpy scipy

# Install all at once from requirements file:
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Check what's installed:
pip list

# Save installed packages to a file:
pip freeze > requirements.txt

# STEP 7: DEACTIVATE the virtual environment
deactivate
# (venv) disappears from prompt — back to global Python

# STEP 8: RE-ACTIVATE anytime
cd C:\Users\YourName\Documents\genai_project
venv\Scripts\activate
```

## Create `.env` File for API Keys (Best Practice!)

```
```bash
# Create .env file in your project root
# genai_project/.env

# NEVER commit this file to Git!
# Add .env to .gitignore
```

```ini
# .env file contents:
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
GROQ_API_KEY=gsk_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

```bash
# Install python-dotenv to load .env file
pip install python-dotenv
```

```python
# load_env.py — Use this at top of ALL your scripts
from dotenv import load_dotenv
import os

load_dotenv()  # Loads .env file automatically

OPENAI_API_KEY   = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
GROQ_API_KEY     = os.getenv("GROQ_API_KEY")
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")

print("Keys loaded successfully!")
```
